names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 11 Μαρτίου, «Όσιος Γεώργιος ο Σιναΐτης», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 11 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Преподобни Георгије Синаит.“, with the rank word Преподобни left off. Синаит is kept: it is the epithet of his mountain, it is what this folder's English name already carries from the Greek calendar, and a bare Георгије would fold with a great many folders.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 11ης Μαρτίου — «Όσιος Γεώργιος ο Σιναΐτης»

attestations.note: The page puts him under Justinian I «(527 - 565 μ.Χ.)» and while Peter I «(524 - 552 μ.Χ.)» was patriarch of Jerusalem, has him a monk of mount Sinai, and tells the miracle of his coming to the church of the Resurrection and back to his cell; it says he and the patriarch reposed peacefully together six months later, as he had foretold. It gives no year and no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 24.03.2026 (11. март ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Георгије Синаит.“

attestations.note: The day's third and last entry, four sentences long. It calls him игуман of the mountain of Sinai, which is a rank the folder did not hold, so `abbot` was added to its `types`; the folder's `floruit` under Justinian is narrower than the Prologue's bare sixth century and was left exactly as it was, since a reading does not widen a sourced interval any more than it narrows one.

floruit.note: saint.gr: «Ο Όσιος Γεώργιος έζησε στα χρόνια του βασιλιά Ιουστινιανού του Α' (527 - 565 μ.Χ.) και όταν Πατριάρχης Ιεροσολύμων ήταν ο Πέτρος ο Α' (524 - 552 μ.Χ.)». The interval is where the two reigns the page prints overlap; it gives no year of its own.
